## Bottom line
**Suggests Benign (62%)** · Unreliable input · Careful review
Image is atypical (98th percentile) and Normal is also in the 90% set [F1].

## Confidence
| Signal | Value | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| Top probabilities | Benign 62%, Normal 38% | Two-way split |
| Conformal set | Normal, Benign | Cannot separate them |
| Reliability / OOD | 0.76 / 98th pct | Flagged, atypical image |
| Second-model (MUSK) agreement | No | Top classes differ |
| Similar cases | 1 of 5 Benign | Neighbors mostly Normal |

## Tissue evidence
- **Normal lobules** (regions 0, 10, 11) · ↓ invasive · Largest lowering association in concept model · Unreliable
- **Gland / tubule formation** (regions 2, 4, 7) · ↓ invasive · Associated with lower invasive likelihood [F3] · Validated
- **Tumor infiltrating stroma** (regions 5, 11) · ↑ invasive · Associated with invasion; P(invasive) still under 1% [F4] · Validated
- **Nuclear size** (regions 3, 5, 8) · context · Smallest in reference set (40 µm², 0th percentile) [F7] · Measured

## Trust check
- **Heatmap**: Removing top 3 regions drops invasive logit 0.54 more than random (CI 0.47–0.60): faithful.
- **Concepts**: Deletion CI includes 0 (−0.005 to 0.007): not shown to reflect classifier. Normal lobules is Unreliable (0/20).

## Could be wrong if
- Image is atypical (98th percentile OOD), so 62% may be miscalibrated.
- Second model (MUSK) disagrees, so the Benign-Normal split may not hold.

## Check on the slide
1. **Regions 5, 11:** Is the stroma truly tumor-infiltrated, or reactive benign stroma?
2. **Regions 0, 10, 11:** Confirm two-layered lobules yourself; AI spot check failed (0/20).
3. **Regions 3, 5, 8:** Check focus and stain; nuclei look unusually small.
